title: Shifting a Reflected Square Root Graph to the Right
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: The graph of y = -sqrt(x) is to be shifted right 3 units. Give an equation for the shifted graph and describe the original and shifted curves.

steps.title: Apply the Rightward Horizontal Shift Rule
steps.explanation: To shift the graph of y = -sqrt(x) to the right by 3 units, replace x with x - 3.
steps.why: A horizontal shift right by c > 0 units replaces x with x - c.

steps.title: Determine the Shifted Domain and Range
steps.explanation: Requiring the radicand x - 3 >= 0 gives the domain [3, infinity). Since the principal square root is negated, the outputs cover (-infinity, 0].
steps.why: Horizontal translation shifts the domain from [0, infinity) to [3, infinity) while preserving the range (-infinity, 0].

steps.title: Identify Key Points for Sketching
steps.explanation: The original curve y = -sqrt(x) begins at (0, 0) and descends into the fourth quadrant through (1, -1) and (4, -2). The shifted curve begins at (3, 0) and descends through (4, -1) and (7, -2).
steps.why: Adding 3 to each x-coordinate translates all points of y = -sqrt(x) three units to the right.
